description: Sanderstead Library, built in 1936 in the moderne style, was closed since late 2024. A year ago, it reopens for the first time on Open House Weekend as the future home of The Story Sanctuary - a creative health and wellbeing hub in the making. A year on, come down and see how things have developed, learn more about our plans for the building and the future of this precious community space.

factsheet.heading: Building and History
paragraphs: Sanderstead library is unusual in that it is the style of an open book with the spine being the main entrance and two small 'wings'.  It has large Crittall-style windows at either end and most of the original fitted furniture in situ: the dark wood bookcases in the main library hall and fitted cupboards in the staff room.

Designed by architects Gold and Aldridge in the Moderne style along with Purley, Kenley and Coulsdon as part of a single project. Gold and Aldridge were well known in the interwar years for designing libraries.
Constructed by Messrs Truett and Steel Ltd, of Thornton Heath, a firm who also built many residential houses in Sanderstead, for example in Glebe Hyrst.

factsheet.heading: The Story Sanctuary Plan
paragraphs: “Many things make us human, but our desire to share stories about who we are, where we come from, and what we mean to each other is the most extraordinary and essential.”

We are a few months into our plan to create a space to make, share, rest, laugh, and reconnect – working with local residents and creative and voluntary organisations from across Croydon. From visual arts and writing to movement, song, games, gardening, and more; we aim to gently transform the building into a warm, creative space where everyone feels they belong.

factsheet.heading: Can the tree talk?: Saturday 12th September
paragraphs: As part of the Open House Festival we’ll be opening the doors to everyone to join us to celebrate a year of a community hub in the making and invite our supporters to become members of our cooperative.

As the conclusion of our summer programming, we will be exploring how we create a healthy inclusive space for the human and non-human living creatures who rely on our building and grounds for sanctuary - sharing our plans from cafe to community garden to shared ownership.
